offence_severity: Death sentence (minimum/maximum: not specified, but death sentence awarded)
physical_harm: The boy was murdered by administering an overdose of chloroform and pentazocine
number_of_offences: Four offences charged (ss. 302, 364A, 201 and 120-8), death sentence upheld for two accused, life imprisonment for the lady accused
premeditation_planning: Yes, the court found premeditation/planning as the murder was committed in a pre-planned manner using scientific methods
motive: Ransom, to extract a heavy ransom of Rs.50,00,000/-
key_evidence_accepted: Eye witness to the kidnapping by two accused - Witnesses not chance witnesses - Medical evidence that the cause of death was overdose of chloroform and pentazocine - Evidence to the effect that conspiracy hatched between accused - Attempt by lady accused to destroy the evidence relating to kidnapping - Recovery of various articles including telephone call details, medical equipment and car used as also dead body of deceased
witness_credibility: PW-BS and SK were natural at the places they professed to be in and cannot be dubbed as chance witnesses. BS gave a cogent explanation as to the circumstances under which he had seen AV being kidnapped and taken away. SK was not in any way connected with RV-complainant and they were not even known to each other.
post_offence_conduct: The appellants were under grave suspicion, suspected to be accused in a case of kidnapping and murder, and VS and JS had attempted to run away and S was in the process of destroying evidence, when they had been apprehended and put in police custody
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 14.02.2005; Trial judgment: 30.5.2008; High Court decision: Not stated; Supreme Court decision: 25.01.2010
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Not stated; Counsel for the State: Not stated
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and death sentence; High Court: Upheld death sentence; Supreme Court: Affirmed death sentence for two accused, commuted to life imprisonment for the lady accused
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the two appellants-VS and JS kidnapped AV-a school boy aged 16 years from his school in the car for ransom. During the negotiations, the kidnappers administered heavy doses of chloroform and fortwin injections to the boy which resulted in his death. The appellants-VS and JS had attempted to run away and the appellant S-wife of JS, was in the process of destroying the evidence relating to kidnapping when they were apprehended by the police.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the appellants were young persons, and Sonia a lady as well, who could be rehabilitated and that the pre-dominant trend being against the imposition of the death penalty as of today, and the evidence being circumstantial in nature, the death penalty should not be awarded.
legal_principle_applied: The legal principle applied was the 'rarest of the rare cases' test, which requires that the death penalty be awarded only in exceptional circumstances where the crime is particularly heinous and the accused's conduct is extremely grave.
precedent_relied_upon: Bachan Singh vs. State of Punjab (1980) 2 SCC 684; Henry Westmuller Roberts vs. State of Assam (1985) 3 SCC 291; Rana Partap & Ors. vs. State of Haryana 1983(3) SCC 327; State of Himachal Pradesh vs. K.L.Pardhan & Ors. 1987 (2) SCC 17; Keshar Singh & Ors. vs. State (Delhi Administration) 1988 (3) SCC 609; State of Uttar Pradesh vs. Deoman Upadhyaya AIR 1960 SC 1125; Narayan Swami vs. Emperor AIR 1939 PC 47; Sushi Kumar vs. State of Punjab Criminal Appeal No.670 of 2009; Mohan & Ors. vs. State of T.N. (1998) 5 SCC 336
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the case involved the kidnapping of a school-going innocent boy for ransom and the murder of the boy in a pre-planned manner using scientific methods and administering fatal doses of chemicals. The court found that the crime was particularly heinous and that the death penalty was necessary to deter such crimes.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The court considered that Sonia, the lady appellant, may have been under pressure from her husband and Vikram Singh and was not present at the time of the kidnapping, which led to some leniency being shown to her.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The court weighed the aggravating factors such as the pre-planned nature of the kidnapping and murder, the use of scientific methods to ensure the crime went undetected, and the fact that the deceased was a young boy who was tortured and killed in a brutal manner.
other_sentence_order: The court commuted the death sentence of the lady accused, Sonia, to life imprisonment, and dismissed the appeals of the other two appellants.
